svg.title: A complete forward: preparation, execution, feedback and safe reuse
svg.desc: One request completes a decode token with two recurrent loops. CPU preparation, GPU dependencies, readback, collection and buffer lifetimes share one time axis. The scheduler selects compatible loops from several requests into one batch. Named buffer waits connect directly to the storage they protect. A separate panel shows delayed exit decisions.
svg.text: 02 / One forward. Three kinds of dependency.
CPU may submit ahead. GPU waits for its inputs. Host decisions wait only for the results they consume.
A SAME REQUEST · FULL DECODE TOKEN · TWO FIXED RECURRENT LOOPS
P = PRELUDE R0 / R1 = recurrent depths 0 / 1 C = CODA + sampling P′ = next token’s PRELUDE
Shared vertical lines: wait ends = old input use ends = prior GPU work completes.
W0 ends: P done / buffer 0 released
W1 ends: R0 done / buffer 1 released
W2 ends: R1 done / buffer 0 released
The next prep and buffer write start at that boundary. Host wake-up overhead is omitted; widths are illustrative.
GPU arrows: hidden / KV / sampled token stay on device. No collect between P, R0 and R1.
P / R0 / R1: no host result in this fixed-depth example.
C submission queues P′ using the device token; collection decides stop / continue.
C result storage held until collect releases it
Input reuse follows compute completion. D2H completion makes output readable; collect releases its lease.
P′ may run before EOS is known; the next CODA must resolve the preceding token’s stop decision.
B MANY REQUESTS → ONE RECURRENT BATCH → PER-REQUEST PROGRESS
Per-request positions, KV and row ranges
B → CODA queue · if exit is established
Each request advances separately. The scheduler selects the next batch again; membership is not fixed.
Example order follows decode then prefill selection. PRELUDE / CODA are not mixed into this recurrent batch.
D / E are independent ready requests; no collect of A / B / C is needed just to prepare their batch.
The rotating input buffers belong to batch submissions. Previous readers still protect each buffer before reuse.
C DATA-DEPENDENT EXIT · THE DELAYED POLICY CHANGES THE HOST DEPENDENCY
Submit R1 first; consume g0 to allow R2 or enqueue CODA. This is the configured delayed-exit semantics.
If g0 is required and not readable, collect waits. Fixed-depth / trace / maximum-depth paths can skip it.
Split prefill: each chunk follows P → R0 → … → Rlast; only prompt completion proceeds to CODA.
Atomic prefill may fuse P + recurrent loops into one submission. Each input tensor owner has its own pool.
One GPU lane is shown; multi-stream execution remains optional. Time widths are illustrative. Draft/verify uses its own round controller.
